heading: Self-repair is partial, varies across prompts, and can overcompensate
definition: compensation is partial on average, varies widely by prompt, and sometimes overcorrects beyond the original effect.
summary: Partial compensation has independent support. Wide variation and occasional overcompensation remain supported only by the original researchers.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: 'partial' is R2 (arXiv:2607.01940, GPT-2-small IOI, non-original group); prompt variation and overcorrection are R0 (only original arXiv:2402.15390, Pythia-410M and Pythia-160M). 1-10B: R0, rows only from the originals (Chinchilla 7B in arXiv:2307.15771, Pythia-1B in arXiv:2402.15390); arXiv:2610.02173's text-based support has no rows and no size in the pack. Toy, 10-100B and >100B: no V4 evidence (counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size).
suggested_status.reason: The statement has three parts. Partial restoration is reported by the originals (arXiv:2307.15771#R3, arXiv:2307.15771#R5; arXiv:2402.15390#R6; counts: versions.V4.original_sources_linked) and independently supported by arXiv:2607.01940#r1 (GPT-2-small IOI) and arXiv:2610.02173 (text-based contrastive-swap results, Appendix H and Section I.5; no V4 rows). counts: versions.V4.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original is 0. Partial restoration alone warrants R2. Prompt variation and overcorrection remain supported only by original arXiv:2402.15390 (arXiv:2402.15390#R8, arXiv:2402.15390#R9; Section 2.3; arXiv:2402.15390#R18). arXiv:2610.02173 does not directly test prompt-level compensation spread or overcorrection; its coupling-and-dose account proposes a mechanism for variability and does not demonstrate a limitation of V4. Its limits_scope label should therefore be none. counts: versions.V4.verdicts retains that superseded label and should not be treated as evidence against prompt variability. The complete claim remains R0.
suggested_status.open_questions: Independent measurements of per-prompt compensation spread under resample ablation and of overcorrection beyond the original effect would move those components toward R2. A dose-matched comparison could clarify how coupling and pair-dependent dose contribute to variability; a dose explanation alone would not establish C. Independent V4 tests at 1-10B and tests at toy, 10-100B or >100B would extend the scale-specific assessment (counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size).

source.title: Explorations of Self-Repair in Language Models

original_result.setup: The researchers ablated individual attention heads on The Pile and compared heads' direct contributions to output logits with changes in the correct token's logit after ablation.
original_result.result: Pythia-1B showed partial repair, while Pythia-410M varied substantially across 5000 tokens despite average repair. In Pythia-160M, setting a head's output to zero (zero ablation) could increase the correct-token logit difference even when that head's direct contribution was positive.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: GPT-2-small recovered much, but not all, function lost by ablating three primary name-copying attention heads.
Recruited backups restored only part of the erased effect in instruct and base models.
The authors attributed ablation-induced variation to coupling and pair-dependent intervention doses.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: No study outside the originals quantifies the per-prompt spread of compensation.
untested.basis: 'Untested parts of V4' lines: arXiv:2607.01940 says prompt-level variation is not reported; arXiv:2610.02173 says per-prompt spread is not reported directly; arXiv:2307.15771 says variability appears only in scatter plots and is not quantified. The checker confirms that fixed-dose per-prompt compensation spread is untested in arXiv:2610.02173. Its coupling-and-dose explanation proposes a mechanism for variation; it does not demonstrate a limitation of descriptive prompt variability. counts: versions.V4.coverage_by_operation.removal does not distinguish fixed-dose prompt-spread measurements.

untested.what: Scale coverage: no V4 evidence at toy, 10-100B or >100B scale. The 1-10B rows come only from the originals (Chinchilla 7B, Pythia-1B).
untested.basis: counts: versions.V4.studies_by_size (1-10B 2, <1B 2) and versions.V4.coverage_by_operation.removal.by_size (1-10B 2, <1B 2). The 1-10B rows are arXiv:2307.15771#R3, #R5 and arXiv:2402.15390#R6.

Fixed-dose per-prompt spread and overcorrection remain untested in that study. No Llama V4 result is identified in the supplied synthesis.

untested.what: Independent replication of overcorrection beyond the original effect remains untested in the supplied synthesis.
untested.basis: V4.wording_issues[1] and the 'untested parts of V4' lines identify no overcorrection measurement in arXiv:2307.15771, arXiv:2607.01940 or arXiv:2610.02173. The checker confirms original arXiv:2402.15390 reports overcorrection during resample-ablation analysis (Section 2.3) and explicitly demonstrates zero-ablation overcorrection (Section 3.2, Figure 5; arXiv:2402.15390#R18, corrected to observed for V4): positive logit differences can occur despite positive clean head direct effects. counts: versions.V4.original_sources_linked identifies arXiv:2402.15390 as an original; versions.V4.rows_by_state does not distinguish independent overcorrection tests and retains R18's superseded cannot_determine state.

wording_issues.issue: The studies measure different quantities at different units (layer, head, head set, direction or unit). Chinchilla 7B: about 70% of the token-logit reduction at middle layers is restored under resample ablation, combining attention compensation with reduced MLP erasure (arXiv:2307.15771#R5). Under contrastive swaps, arXiv:2610.02173 reports recruited-backup restoration of the erased verdict: Gemma instruct/base 6–9%/11–13%, Qwen 9–10%/22–27%, and Mistral 8–11%/24–25% (Appendix H, text-based). GPT-2-small IOI: margin 2.574 to 2.290 after jointly zero-ablating primary name movers with a +2.52 direct contribution (arXiv:2607.01940#r1). For Pythia-410M L20H14 under resample ablation, the authors suggest possible near-full repair (arXiv:2402.15390#R11). The statement specifies neither the measure nor the population being averaged.

method_sensitivity.factor: ablation type and dose (zero, mean, resample; contrastive swap dose ladder)
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2610.02173: mean, zero and resample clamps place each prompt pair at a different dose (mean ablation up to |λ|=5.1), compared with a prompt-matched contrastive swap dose ladder on a zero-shot binary factual-verdict task with one answer position and a small IOI head bench. Responses differ by model, direction and dose; joint-core interventions can recruit more than single-core ones; the response saturates beyond full inversion. Under the authors' affine model, variation depends on coupling and dose spread (Section 7, Appendices N–O). This does not demonstrate a limitation of V4's descriptive prompt variability; fixed-dose per-prompt spread and overcorrection remain untested. arXiv:2402.15390: the LayerNorm contribution depends on the ablation method. Zero-ablating Pythia-160M L11H0 can produce positive logit differences despite positive clean head direct effects, showing observed overcorrection for V4 (R18).

arXiv:2402.15390 (method-sensitivity line): the reported self-repair fraction depends materially on filtering to high-direct-effect tokens and on per-token clipping. Its Pythia-1B layer summary uses the top 2% of tokens by head direct effect (R6).

arXiv:2307.15771, Chinchilla 7B: direct and compensatory effects are well correlated mainly at intermediate layers. Early layers have a large total effect but little direct effect; the line on very late layers is truncated in the pack. The regression slope is below one at all layers past layer 13 (R3), and about 70% restoration is reported at middle layers (R5).

arXiv:2402.15390, Pythia-410M on 5000 Pile tokens: L22H11 and L20H6 show substantial token-level variation (R8, R9, observed), while L23H1 and L20H14 show no clear correlation between direct effect and logit change (R10, R11, cannot_determine). The method-sensitivity line says self-repair varies substantially by prompt and by head.

arXiv:2610.02173 (verdict reason, text-based, App. H): under the core swap, recruited backups restore the following percentages of the erased verdict: Gemma instruct 6–9%, base 11–13%; Qwen instruct 9–10%, base 22–27%; Mistral instruct 8–11%, base 24–25%.

method_sensitivity.factor: choice of primary set and replacement operator
method_sensitivity.what: arXiv:2607.01940 (method-sensitivity line): backup recovery varies with the identity and contamination of the supplied primary set, the ablation replacement operator, the output geometry and the task or prompt setting. Joint and summed ablation effects differ (Appendix C.4.3, Table 20). Those numbers are only in a 'not in rows' line, so they are not stated here.
